chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was visited in the mosque, and it was said to him, 'A predator among the birds is upon the Kaaba; nothing from the doves of the Sanctuary passes by it except that it strikes it.' So he said, 'Set up a trap for it and kill it, for it has become a heretic.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing birds that disturb the peace of the Kaaba according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies a predatory bird disrupting the sanctuary's doves as having committed *al-had* (heresy/deviation), extending the concept of religious transgression to creatures that violate the sanctity of the Haram. This incident highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that *al-had* is not limited to humans but can apply to animals whose actions disrupt the sacred order, justifying their removal or killing as a form of enforcing the sanctity of the holy site.
